reflexion_entries_to_archive.note: S135 P0. My hunter-lifetime mutation matrix reported a FALSE all-green on its first run — every mutation showed failCount 0 while STAYING GREEN — the exact S134 disease one session later. This time I had built TWO independent detectors into the harness: a per-test x/✗ scan AND a summary 'Tests N failed' regex. They DISAGREED (the x-scan found [TEST A,B,C] failing while failCount read 0), and that disagreement is what exposed the real bug: ANSI colour codes broke the summary regex, not the mutations. Fix was to key the RED signal off execSync's non-zero exit, not a fragile summary parse. LESSON: a single pass/fail parser of tool output is untrustworthy; build a second, differently-shaped detector and treat any disagreement between them as 'my harness is lying', not 'the code passed'. The redundancy, not my judgement, caught it.

S135 P0. My draft test plan said 'seed a hunter via makeHunter and assert hashWorldStateFull equality'. The TEST agent (disk-grounded) found that restore reconstructs nextHunterId=maxId+1 while a raw-seeded source stays at 0, and nextHunterId is hashed — so the equality would have been a FALSE-RED that no correct fix could turn green, pressuring a later session to weaken the assertion. Seeding via applySpawnHunter (which advances the same counter) fixes it. LESSON: for any host-vs-successor hash-equality assertion, enumerate EVERY hashed world scalar the rehydrate path reconstructs (nextXId counters, tick, hunterSpawned) and make the source produce them the same way — or the strongest guard becomes an un-passable trap. Verified tick round-trips via applySnapshotCore on BOTH paths before trusting the assertion.
